summary: Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto Monasteries under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. He held professorships at Minzu University, Tibet University, and Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist. Educated at Vidyasagar, Scottish Church, and Calcutta colleges, he served as professor at Scottish Church College (ca. 1939–1952), Sanskrit College and University (from 1952), and the University of Calcutta (ca. 1956–1965).

Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD from the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri, and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.
Dušan Zbavitel (1925–2012) was an Indologist. He studied at Charles University (ca. 1945–1949) under Vincenc Lesný and later held a post there from ca. 1954 to 1968.

Dwarikadas Shastri (born 1922) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Bauddhadarśanācārya degree at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, founded Bauddha Bharati, and served as joint editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwight Whitney Learned (1848–1943) was a scholar in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his BA and PhD at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Thayer College (1872–1875) and Doshisha University (1875–1928).

Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta, he served as Professor of History at the University of Delhi from ca. 1975 to 2005.

Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS and the Catholic University of Louvain (PhD 2018), and held positions at Louvain, Ruhr University Bochum (2019–2022), and 84000 (2022).

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo, Tulku Urgyen, and Khenpo Rinchen. In 1990, he was a Buddhist philosophy professor at Naropa University.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded the Nitartha Institute, serving as its director around 1996.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.
Dániel Balogh works in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He has held positions at the British Museum (attested 2021) and as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).
Dávid Jónás is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Tibetology. He received his PhD from Eötvös Loránd University in 2019 and became an assistant lecturer there in 2021.

Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

E. Adelaide Hahn (1893–1967) was a linguist who studied at Hunter College and Columbia University under Edgar H. Sturtevant, Leonard Bloomfield, and Franklin Edgerton. She taught at Hunter College (1915–1963) and was Linguistic Society of America president (1946).

E. Baer was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Basel and the University of Zurich (PhD), where his teachers included Adolf Kaegi, Jakob Hausheer, Eduard Schwyzer, and Emil Abegg.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry (born 1930) is an Indology scholar who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. He was appointed a lecturer in the Sanskrit department at the University of Kerala around 1965.

E. F. Schumacher (1911–1977) was a scholar in philosophy. He studied at the University of Bonn, New College, LSE, and Columbia University, and under Edward Conze. He held academic posts at Columbia (ca. 1932–1934) and Oxford (ca. 1942–1944).

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, Utah, and Washington under Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche. He held posts at the Library of Congress and Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
E. H. Hall was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under George Abraham Grierson and served as a clerk at the India Office Records.
